tips.title: Airbrushing Vallejo Model Air — Thinning Ratio and Pressure
tips.text: Vallejo Model Air is thin enough for airbrushing without dilution. However, adding Vallejo Airbrush Thinner at a 1:2 ratio improves flow and atomization. Add 2-3 drops of Vallejo Flow Improver per 10 drops of thinned paint for better flow. Spray at 1.5-2.0 bar pressure for a consistent, fine mist. Test paint consistency on a white plastic plate.

tips.title: Base Coat Technique — Alclad II Primer and Vallejo
tips.text: Begin by applying Alclad II Primer with an Iwata HP-BCS airbrush at 1.5 bar pressure. Light coats are key — aim for semi-opaque coverage. Let dry for 15 minutes. Next, apply Vallejo Model Color base coat using the same pressure. Start with light coats, building up opacity gradually. Allow 24 hours drying time between coats.

tips.title: Camouflage Masking — Eduard PE Masks and Tamiya Tape
tips.text: For complex camouflage patterns, use Eduard PE masks. Apply with tweezers, pressing gently onto the model. For larger areas, use Tamiya masking tape. Cut precise patterns using GodHand nippers and tweezers. Apply with firm, steady pressure to prevent paint bleed. Remove masks immediately after painting to avoid damaging the paint.

tips.title: Applying AK Interactive Washes — Dilution and Application
tips.text: AK Interactive Washes are concentrated — dilute with AK Interactive Wash Medium at a 1:3 ratio for better control. Apply washes with a soft, flat brush, working from top to bottom and sides to center. Allow washes to sit for 15-30 seconds before removing excess with a clean, damp brush. Blot dry with a paper towel. Washes add depth and panel line definition.

tips.title: Chipping with Sponge Technique — Tamiya Acrylics and AMMO
tips.text: Chipping requires planning — decide where to apply chips, typically around edges and areas subject to wear. Apply AMMO by Mig Jimenez Weathering Master Chips first, allowing it to dry for 15 minutes. Lightly dab a damp sponge into Tamiya Acrylic paint matching the underlying color. Gently dab chips onto the model. Remove excess AMMO with a damp cloth before it dries completely.
